title: Why the Shady Side of the Street Feels Cooler
title_ja: 街路樹の日陰はなぜ涼しいのか

source_links.title: U.S. EPA: Frequent Heat Island Questions and Resources

fact_notes: 米国環境保護庁が説明する都市のヒートアイランド現象を背景にした架空の学校調査。地域差を無視した定量的な冷却効果は主張しない。

sentences.en: On a summer afternoon, students walk along two streets that are only a short distance apart.
sentences.ja: 夏の午後、生徒たちは少ししか離れていない二つの通りを歩きます。

sentences.en: One street has wide sidewalks beside buildings, while the other has rows of mature trees.
sentences.ja: 一方には建物沿いの広い歩道があり、もう一方には大きく育った木が並びます。

sentences.en: Although the air temperature may be similar, the students feel more comfortable under the trees.
sentences.ja: 気温は似ていても、生徒たちは木の下の方が快適に感じます。

sentences.en: The difference raises a practical question about how cities can protect people during hot weather.
sentences.ja: この違いは、暑い天候で都市が人々をどう守るかという現実的な問いを生みます。

sentences.en: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency explains that buildings and paved surfaces absorb and hold heat.
sentences.ja: 米国環境保護庁は建物や舗装面が熱を吸収し保持すると説明します。

sentences.en: As a result, developed areas can become warmer than the surrounding countryside, an effect known as an urban heat island.
sentences.ja: その結果、開発された地域は周辺の田園地帯より暑くなり、これは都市ヒートアイランドと呼ばれます。

sentences.en: Trees may reduce the amount of sunlight that reaches a sidewalk or a wall.
sentences.ja: 木々は歩道や壁に届く日光の量を減らせます。

sentences.en: Leaves also release water into the air, which can help cool the surrounding environment.
sentences.ja: 葉は空気中に水分も放出し、周辺環境を冷やす助けになります。

sentences.en: For example, a bench beneath a large tree can offer a more pleasant resting place than a bench in direct sunlight.
sentences.ja: 例えば大きな木の下のベンチは、直射日光下のベンチより快適な休憩場所になり得ます。

sentences.en: However, the cooling effect depends on the tree species, its size, and local conditions.
sentences.ja: しかし冷却効果は樹種、大きさ、地域条件によって変わります。

sentences.en: A newly planted tree cannot provide exactly the same shade as one that has grown for decades.
sentences.ja: 新しく植えた木は何十年も育った木とまったく同じ日陰を作れません。

sentences.en: It is therefore misleading to assume that planting any tree will immediately solve a city's heat problems.
sentences.ja: したがってどんな木でも植えれば都市の暑さを直ちに解決できると考えるのは誤解を招きます。

sentences.en: A city planning department must consider more than the number of trees it plants.
sentences.ja: 都市計画部門は植える木の本数以外も考慮しなければなりません。

sentences.en: Roots need suitable soil and enough space, while branches may require care near roads and power lines.
sentences.ja: 根には適した土と空間が必要で、枝は道路や電線の近くでは手入れが必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: In addition, residents need clear paths that remain accessible to wheelchair users and people with strollers.
sentences.ja: さらに住民には車いす利用者やベビーカー利用者も通れる道が必要です。

sentences.en: Trees that are planted without enough space may damage pavement or struggle to grow.
sentences.ja: 十分な空間なしに植えられた木は舗装を傷めたり、育ちにくくなったりするかもしれません。

sentences.en: A responsible plan includes long-term maintenance rather than treating planting day as the end of the project.
sentences.ja: 責任ある計画では植樹の日を活動の終わりとせず、長期的な維持管理を含めます。

sentences.en: Listening to local people can reveal where shade is especially important during daily travel.
sentences.ja: 地域住民の声を聞くと日々の移動で日陰が特に必要な場所が見えてきます。

sentences.en: Students can investigate the issue by comparing safe locations at similar times of day.
sentences.ja: 生徒は同じような時間帯の安全な場所を比較して調べられます。

sentences.en: They could record whether a place has shade, what materials cover the ground, and how people use it.
sentences.ja: 日陰の有無、地面の素材、人々の使い方を記録できます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, a single measurement cannot establish the effect of every tree in every season.
sentences.ja: それでも一つの測定で全季節のすべての木の効果を証明することはできません。

sentences.en: Careful comparisons should describe conditions and acknowledge other factors such as wind or cloud cover.
sentences.ja: 慎重な比較では条件を記述し、風や雲量などの別の要因も認めるべきです。

sentences.en: The purpose of the investigation is not simply to find a cooler spot but to understand which changes could make public spaces safer.
sentences.ja: 調査の目的は涼しい場所を見つけるだけでなく、公共空間をより安全にできる変更を理解することです。

sentences.en: A thoughtful city treats trees as living infrastructure that needs both protection and planning.
sentences.ja: 思慮深い都市は木々を保護と計画の両方を必要とする生きたインフラとして扱います。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why every street should have identical trees.
How trees can help cool cities when planting and maintenance are planned carefully.
Why buildings must be removed from cities.
Why cities are always cooler than the countryside.
questions.explanation_ja: 街路樹の冷却効果と長期的な管理が主題です。

questions.prompt: What helps create urban heat islands?
questions.explanation_ja: 建物と舗装面による熱の吸収が説明されます。

questions.prompt: Why may the same air temperature feel different on two streets?
options: One street may have more direct sunlight and less shade.
Trees always change the weather forecast.
Students cannot feel changes in heat.
questions.explanation_ja: 日陰によって直接受ける日射などが異なるためです。

questions.prompt: What happens when leaves release water into the air?
options: The process may help cool the surroundings.
questions.explanation_ja: 葉から水分が放出され周囲を冷やすことがあります。

questions.prompt: Why might a new tree provide less cooling than a mature tree?
options: It is always a different color.
Its size and shade may be smaller.
It is never planted near roads.
questions.explanation_ja: 成長した木とは日陰の広さが異なります。

questions.prompt: Why is the number of trees alone an incomplete planning measure?
options: All tree species grow at the same speed.
Space, soil, accessibility, and care also matter.
questions.explanation_ja: 樹種・場所・維持管理や通行のしやすさも重要です。

options: Work needed to keep something in good condition.

questions.prompt: Whose needs are mentioned when planning clear paths?
options: Wheelchair users and people with strollers.
questions.explanation_ja: 車いす利用者とベビーカー利用者が挙げられます。

questions.prompt: Why should students note wind and cloud cover?
options: To make the project more expensive.
Other factors may affect their comparisons.
questions.explanation_ja: 他の要因が比較結果に影響し得るためです。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence emphasize?
options: Trees should replace all city buildings.
Urban trees need long-term protection and thoughtful planning.
Every public space must become a forest.
questions.explanation_ja: 樹木を生きたインフラとして長期的に管理すべきという結論です。

grammar.explanation_ja: 関係代名詞whichが前の内容に補足を加えています。

grammar.focus: Trees that are planted without enough space
grammar.explanation_ja: 関係代名詞thatと受動態がTreesを修飾します。

grammar.explanation_ja: cannot＋動詞で測定の限界を示します。

冷却の利点から条件による差に転換します。
